d: Imagery of child sexual abuse is uploaded, stored or traded. Any service that hosts images or video will be targeted, whatever its intended audience.
Adults build trust with children in private, then push for images, meetings or a move to another app.
Young users see sexual, violent or otherwise mature content, often pushed to them by recommendations or generated on request.

n: Under-age users on an adult-only service
d: Self-declared age is easy to lie about. Children end up in spaces designed for adults.

n: Unlawful collection or use of children's data
d: Children's personal data is collected, profiled or shared without the consent and protections the law requires.

n: Manipulative design and compulsive use by young users
d: Streaks, endless feeds and spending mechanics exploit young users' developing self-control.
Victims are pressured into sharing intimate images, then blackmailed for money or more images. Organized gangs run this at scale.
Intimate images, including sexual deepfakes, are shared without the consent of the person shown.

n: Sex trafficking and commercial sexual exploitation
d: People, including minors, are advertised, recruited or coerced into commercial sex through the platform.
People receive explicit images or sexual messages they didn't ask for.
Romance, investment, fake job and fake support scams. Scammers build trust, then ask for money, often moving victims off the platform.
Customers are tricked into sending money themselves, for example to someone posing as their bank, a seller or a romantic partner.

n: Non-delivery, counterfeit and misrepresented goods or services
d: Buyers pay and receive nothing, receive fakes, or get something different from what was listed.
Stolen payment details are used to buy things or move money, leaving you with chargebacks, fees and processor penalties.
Fake accounts farm sign-up bonuses, referral rewards and promo codes.

n: Impersonation of people, brands or your staff
d: Accounts pose as real people, popular creators, brands or your own support team to deceive users.
Self-serve ads promote scams, prohibited products, or target people in discriminatory ways.
Criminal proceeds are moved and disguised through accounts, transactions, stored value or items on your platform.
Criminals recruit people, often young, to receive and pass on stolen money, or rent their verified accounts.
Money or services reach sanctioned people, organizations or countries.
Customers in difficult circumstances take on unaffordable debt, lose savings to speculation or are financially abused by others.
Attackers take over accounts through stolen passwords, phishing, SIM swaps or weak recovery flows.
Users are sent malicious files or phishing links through your product.
Individuals are targeted with abuse, threats or coordinated pile-ons.
Content that attacks people for protected characteristics such as race, religion, gender, sexuality or disability.

n: Discrimination by hosts, providers or algorithms
d: People are refused service, charged more or shown different opportunities because of who they are.
Propaganda, recruitment and attack footage from terrorist and violent extremist groups.
Shocking imagery reaches people who didn't choose to see it.
Threats against individuals, schools or places that may be carried out.
Content or conversations that encourage, instruct or glamorize suicide, self-harm or disordered eating.
Trends that encourage young people to do risky things on camera.
False medical claims, dangerous treatments or bad advice presented as fact.

n: Doxxing and exposure of personal information
d: Someone's home address, phone number, workplace or other private details are published to target them.

n: Scraping and bulk harvesting of user data
d: Bots collect profiles and content at scale for spam, fraud, surveillance or resale.

n: Staff or contractor misuse of user data
d: People with internal access look up, leak or misuse private data.

n: Hidden cameras and privacy violations in rentals
d: Guests are recorded without their knowledge.
Someone's location is used to follow, find or harm them.

n: Assault or harm during in-person meetings
d: Physical or sexual violence when people meet, visit or provide services face to face.

n: Harm to workers and service providers
d: Drivers, couriers, hosts and freelancers face assault, harassment or unsafe situations from customers.

n: Unvetted people working under someone else's account
d: Verified workers rent or share their accounts, so the person who shows up hasn't been checked.

n: Fake and bot accounts at scale
d: Automated or mass-created accounts used for spam, fraud, manipulation or reward farming.
Unwanted promotional content and links flood conversations and feeds.
Bought, swapped or self-written reviews mislead customers; honest reviews get suppressed.
Networks of fake or coordinated accounts push narratives, products or political disinformation.
Developers or bots use your API to spam, scrape or manipulate at scale.
Guests can't be warned, banned or held to account. Removed users come straight back, and reports lack evidence of who did what.

n: Drugs, weapons and other prohibited goods
d: Sale or promotion of illegal drugs, weapons, counterfeit documents and other prohibited items.
Counterfeit goods and pirated content expose you to rights-holder claims.
Loot boxes, skin betting or unlicensed gambling, including by minors.
The model is prompted to produce sexualized imagery or text involving children.

n: Deceptive or sexual deepfakes of real people
d: Synthetic media of real people used for harassment, fraud or disinformation.
Users get around safeguards to obtain weapons, hacking or self-harm instructions.

n: Emotional dependency and harmful AI companion responses
d: People form intense attachments to an AI that may encourage isolation, validate harmful ideas or mishandle a crisis.

n: Prompt injection and AI agent misuse
d: Instructions hidden in content hijack the AI to leak data or take unwanted actions.

n: No one owns urgent safety escalations
d: A child-safety report, credible threat or live incident arrives and nobody is responsible for acting on it.

n: Unprepared for law-enforcement and emergency requests
d: Police request data or an emergency disclosure, and there is no process to verify and respond.
Reviewers see graphic, sexual or violent material that harms their mental health.
Mistaken removals and bans with no explanation or appeal erode trust and breach some laws.
